Bayesian Response-Surface Modeling, Geometry, and Optimization

bayesian-rsm-1.1.Rd

Fit-ready first- and second-order Bayesian response surfaces, transformed pseudoquadratic fertilizer models, draw-by-draw canonical geometry, bounded biological and economic optima, steepest and ridge paths, and multiresponse desirability.

bayes_rsm(data, response, factors = NULL, order = 2L,
  family = c("gaussian", "student"))

bayes_pseudoquadratic(data, response, factors, powers = 0.5,
  family = c("gaussian", "student"))

bayes_rsm_canonical(fit, level = 0.95, tolerance = 1e-8,
  max_draws = 1000L)

bayes_rsm_optimum(fit, bounds, goal = c("max", "min"),
  max_draws = 500L, level = 0.95, start = NULL)

bayes_rsm_economic_optimum(fit, bounds, output_price, input_costs,
  fixed_cost = 0, max_draws = 500L, level = 0.95)

bayes_rsm_steepest(fit, direction = c("ascent", "descent"),
  start = NULL, step = 0.25, n_steps = 10L, level = 0.95)

bayes_rsm_ridge(fit, radii = seq(0, 1.5, length.out = 8),
  goal = c("max", "min"), directions = 1000L, seed = 20260826,
  level = 0.95)

bayes_rsm_desirability(fits, specs, bounds, weights = NULL,
  grid_n = 15L, max_draws = 300L, level = 0.95)

Arguments

data

Observed data frame or response-surface design carrying a response.

response

Response column.

factors

Quantitative factor columns.

order

Polynomial order 1 or 2.

family

Gaussian or Student-t response family.

powers

Positive fractional transformation powers.

fit

Fitted response-surface bayes_fit.

level

Credible interval mass.

tolerance

Canonical eigenvalue tolerance.

max_draws

Maximum posterior draws used by a derived analysis.

bounds

Named factor bounds for bounded optimization.

goal

Maximize or minimize.

start

Optional starting point.

output_price

Positive response-unit price.

input_costs

Named factor-unit costs.

fixed_cost

Constant cost.

direction

Steepest ascent or descent.

step

Path step length.

n_steps

Number of path steps.

radii

Radii used for ridge search.

directions

Number of sampled directions per nonzero radius.

seed

Random seed.

fits

Named list of compatible fitted RSM response models.

specs

Named response desirability specifications.

weights

Optional positive response weights.

grid_n

Grid resolution used by desirability optimization.

Value

bayes_rsm() and bayes_pseudoquadratic() return fit-ready bayes_design objects. Derived functions return posterior geometry, path, or bayes_rsm_optimum objects.

Details

Second-order geometry is computed for every retained posterior draw rather than only at the posterior mean. Pseudoquadratic models use an explicit transformed-quadratic definition, \(z_j=x_j^{a_j}\), with linear, squared, and interaction terms in \(z\). This avoids a non-identifiable literal duplication that appears in the printed equation of the 2002 source article. The source ambiguity is documented rather than silently reproduced.

References

Box, G. E. P. and Wilson, K. B. (1951). On the Experimental Attainment of Optimum Conditions. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 13(1), 1–38. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1951.tb00067.x .

Examples

d <- bayes_teaching_data("ccd")
des <- bayes_rsm(d, "yield", c("coded_N", "coded_P"))
fit <- bayes_fit(des, engine = "native", draws = 200)
bayes_rsm_canonical(fit)
#> <bayes_rsm_canonical>
#>   factor     mean    median     lower    upper
#>  coded_N 1.188783 0.8034549 0.4148063 3.214113
#>  coded_P 1.098417 0.5908375 0.1495784 3.183195
#>   Classification probabilities:
#> 
#>       maximum       minimum        saddle ridge_or_flat 
#>             1             0             0             0 
bayes_rsm_optimum(fit, list(coded_N=c(-1.5,1.5), coded_P=c(-1.5,1.5)), max_draws=50)
#> <bayes_rsm_optimum>
#>  quantity      mean    median     lower    upper
#>   coded_N 0.8375991 0.7758457 0.4176930 1.499617
#>   coded_P 0.6532880 0.5146770 0.2560472 1.500000
#>  response 7.7208203 7.7061297 7.3662952 8.356712
#>   Boundary probability: 0.1
